text:
lucy: FYI I'm seeing tenants hit weird deprecation UX after the v2 rollout. the console shows them flagged as "v2-enabled" but traffic is sporadically routed to v1 and the tenant sees a deprecation banner for v1 consumers even though they called v2.

sam: can you paste a sample request/response cycle? are headers/pins being respected?

lucy: minimal trace:
```
# initial handshake (v2)
> POST /v2/generate Authorization: Bearer T-zz X-Api-Version: v2
< 200 OK
< X-Route-Affinity: ra:deadbeef; Max-Age=86400
< X-Served-Variant: v2-quant

# 2 minutes later
> POST /v2/generate Authorization: Bearer T-zz X-Api-Version: v2
< 200 OK
< X-Served-Variant: v1-legacy
< X-Deprecation-Notice: the v1 path will be removed in 90 days
```

rachel: is there any intermediary between the client and our edge that rewrites headers? i.e. CDN or customer proxy?

dylan: looks like a race where the token->route mapping is updated during a rolling deploy and for a short window the central store returns older affinity. edge caches then pick default route (v1). we've seen similar when we made the rollout of variant-mapping async.

sam: did we change the attribution keys for billing recently? that could cause the console to surface deprecation banners incorrectly if telemetry thinks the tenant is v1.

dylan: yes, last week metrics ingestion switched to use served_variant as the primary billing dimension to simplify downstream joins. that was faster but means if a request falls back to v1 the billing/console reflects v1 even if the caller requested v2.

lucy: customers hit a confusing flow: call v2, sometimes get v1, then see a v1 deprecation banner in the console and open a ticket. looks like a UX+compat problem.

ops-bot: deploy: routing-core:release-2026.03.10 applied to region-global at 2026-03-10T22:07Z by @release-ci

sam: mitigation proposal: for the near-term revert metrics attribution to prefer token_origin (derived from Authorization token hash) over served_variant for billing and UI flags. That will keep the console aligned with the tenant's intention while we fix routing stability.
rachel: agree. also add a transient "compat-mode" flag in the console UI that will suppress v1 deprecation banners for tenants with v2 tokens for 48h after a detected route-affinity flip. shows as "suppress deprecation for suspected routing drift".
dylan: routing patch: make token->route mapping writes strongly-consistent during rollout (no async fanout) plus add short-lived shadow write to edge cache with server-side delta-check to avoid stampede. do that as a canary in one region first.
lucy: rollout UX: we should design a canary badge and a small console affordance: when we enable the new route mapping for a tenant show a "Migration in progress" badge and link to details. don't show deprecation banners until mapping has been consistent for X minutes.
sam: owners + timeline:
- metrics (sam): revert billing attr to token_origin (15m) & add backfill job (6h)
- edge (dylan): strong-consistency patch + shadow-cache canary (2h)
- console (rachel): suppress-deprecation flag + migration-badge (1h)
- devex (lucy): customer note + support playbook (30m)

ops-bot: incident-note: routing-deprecation-ux tagged infra/metrics/console/devex priority-high.
rachel: I'll wire a temporary UI toggle under admin -> deploys called "hide v1 deprecation while routing unstable" with a per-tenant timer. keep disabled by default.
dylan: for observability I'll add a metric: route_affinity_consistency{tenant} = fraction of requests in 10m window with api_version==v2 and served_variant==v2. alert if below 99.8% for billing-tier customers.
lucy: also export an event whenever we detect a cross-variant attribution (token_origin==v2 but served_variant==v1) to the audit log. that helps support explain the tickets.
sam: quick check: does reverting metrics attribution have any legal/billing implications? finance? we should cc them before making the rollback global. lucy, can you loop in finance & support?
lucy: looping in @finance and @support now in #support. i'll paste sanitized logs and the proposed language for customer comms: "We've observed transient routing mismatches during a recent rollout; we've temporarily aligned billing/console with your token version while we stabilize routing. No action required on your part."
rachel: once canary looks healthy, let's automate the suppression window so customers don't have to rely on manual toggles. UX copy will make it clear why the banner is hidden and link to the migration status page.
dylan: will post a follow-up with the canary dashboard and logs. aiming for canary in 60m and global after 4 hours if stable.
lucy: thanks team. i'll update thread with support responses and link to the canary dashboard when ready. :thumbsup:
